proven_bounds.claim: no forced BLACK win within 28 plies
proven_bounds.nodes_note: the depth-28 slice; the whole iteratively-deepened run from depth 6 was 189,713,209,576 nodes in 2742.1s (45.7 min). Supersedes a depth-22 bound taken on a 10-core M2 Pro under a long-superseded build.
proven_bounds.method: null-window mate hunt, iterative deepening in one process from depth 6 in steps of 2
proven_bounds.tt: requested cap 2^31 (32 GiB) but ran at 2^30 (16 GiB): growth to 2^31 needs a new 32 GiB block alongside the live 16 GiB and the machine could not spare 48 GiB peak. 100% full from depth 26 on.
proven_bounds.machine: Apple M5 Pro, 18 cores, 64 GiB, macOS (Darwin 25.6.0)
proven_bounds.timing_caveat: the per-depth SECONDS in this run are not comparable with the White run's. Depths through 22 were searched through a stunted 2^20 table caused by a growth bug (fixed in the same session), and the table only reached 2^30 at depth 24, so the depth-22 node count of 2,620,590,190 measures the bug rather than Black's tree, and the d24->d26 growth of x1.5 reflects the table transition rather than the search. The BOUND is unaffected: a null-window hunt returning 0 proves the negative whatever size the table was.

proven_wins_found.pv: 1... Ub4xc2 2. Wb1b2 F@a3 3. Wb2xc2 d3xc2 4. U@b3 Kd4d3 5. Ub3xd2 W@b1#

summary: no forced win for either side within 26 (White) / 28 (Black) plies; game value still open
machine: Both bounds were measured on an Apple M5 Pro, 18 cores, 64 GiB, macOS (Darwin 25.6.0), on the same engine build for the first time.
note: Two claim strengths, not one. A reported mate is a proof of a forced win and, since the TT_BUDGET_GUARD in tinyhouse.c, of the distance it names: the search returns an unsound 0 at the horizon, so a mate score can only come from real terminals. A 'no forced win within N plies' bound is immune to horizon unsoundness, to a TT cutoff overrunning its budget and to store-side graph-history interaction, but not to a 64-bit Zobrist collision, which has no directional structure and could prune a subtree holding a real mate. That residual is unquantified rather than zero; re-run under a second --seed to check it. Deeper bounds: run solve_hunt.py (see README).
reproducibility: The node counts above are NOT exactly reproducible and are not claimed to be. solve_hunt.py defaulted to 2 workers when these runs were made and lazy SMP is nondeterministic, so the worker count in force is not reliably recorded; the default is 1 now, which is deterministic. A cold single-depth run also differs from the iteratively-deepened slice recorded here (a re-run measured +3.4%). The CLAIMS do not depend on any of this: a null-window hunt returning 0 proves the negative whatever the thread count. Reproduce with: solve_hunt.py 0 --tt 31 --workers 16 --maxdepth 26  /  solve_hunt.py 1 --tt 27 --maxdepth 22 (the Black line reproduces the OLD bound; it has not been re-run on the current build or machine, and is now 4 plies behind the White one).
